text:
The Wall Street Journal uncovered new connections in an alleged network smuggling restricted Nvidia *($NVDA)* chips into China, identifying Li Ming as a key operator behind Megaspeed alongside Alice Huang, the former executive romantically linked to Jensen Huang. The investigation found that former Megaspeed associates reportedly now run Novagate Cloud, which received at least $300M in Nvidia-related hardware after Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal no-sell list.

• *Key Operator:* Li allegedly helped direct Megaspeed and related chip-trading businesses behind the scenes. Singapore charged him with fraud in February 2025 for allegedly telling a U.S. supplier that Nvidia-equipped servers were for his local company when they were instead shipped through Malaysia to an undisclosed destination. He remains out on bail.
• *Alice Huang Connections:* Li worked with Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, for years. The couple established Century Longteng in 2021, with Li identified as its chief strategy officer in 2023. The venture was a key shareholder in Shanghai-based Century Litong until 2024.
• *Megaspeed Operations:* Megaspeed gained priority Nvidia chip access in November 2023 after identifying Alibaba *($BABA)* as an anchor customer. It provided legitimate offshore computing services to Alibaba, but the WSJ previously reported that some servers were diverted through Malaysia to Century Litong in violation of U.S. export controls. Megaspeed maintains its business is lawful.
• *New Cloud Operation:* Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal no-sell list in June 2025. Former associates reportedly now operate Novagate Cloud, established in 2025, whose Malaysian entity received at least $300M in Nvidia-equipped hardware during the first five months of 2026. Novagate claims to be an Nvidia cloud partner operating at least two Blackwell-equipped data centers. Corporate records also connect its personnel to Century Litong-associated businesses.
